newsitem.title: USA: Conn. Gov. Rowland scores high approval rating.
newsitem.headline: Conn. Gov. Rowland scores high approval rating.

text.p: Connecticut Governor John Rowland enjoys a high approval rating, but voters are doubtful of his pledge to eliminate the income tax, according to a poll released on Tuesday.
Some 63 percent of those surveyed approve of the job the Republican Rowland is doing, according to a Quinnipiac College Poll.
It's the third time Rowland has topped the 60-percent level, and he also scored higher than the Republican governors of New York and New Jersey.
"Gov. Rowland enjoys widespread support among men and women, in cities, suburbs and rural areas and among all age groups," said Douglas Schwartz, director of the poll.
Even Democrats approved of Rowland by a margin of 50 to 42 percent.

"As he heads into a likely 1998 re-election campaign, Rowland's numbers look good, except for a negative rating on the tough tax question," Schwartz said. "Most Connecticut voters want the income tax eliminated, but they don't think the governor can pull it off."
"Rowland also loses support from those who want to keep the income tax as is," Schwartz said.
Some 67 percent of those surveyed said eliminating the income tax by the year 2000 is a "good idea."
But only 35 percent said it is "very likely" or even "somewhat likely" that Rowland will be able to eliminate the income tax, while 63 percent said it is "not too likely" and "not likely at all."
Respondents also approve of cutting Connecticut's gasoline tax by an 85 to 11 percent margin.
The poll also found that Connecticut's two U.S. senators, Democrats Christopher Dodd and Joe Lieberman, enjoy approval ratings of 54 percent and 66 percent respectively.
Quinnipiac College surveyed 1,059 Connecticut residents who said they were registered voters.
